content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to download a [document] project to a [product_name] using ethernet, but the software can't connect. The download screen does not list any interfaces, and when testing, it only displays 'Connecting' without making progress. If I remove the memory card and use 'Deploy to SD card', then restore to the device, it works, but it's tedious to do this every time. The [document] version is [version_no]. I am using [product_name] [version_no], which works fine and connects without issue. The [product_name] device is [article_no] with a 32GB FAT32 memory card. Any suggestions? Thanks,

Hi [user_name], To assist you further, could you please clarify: 1- Can you ping the [product_name]? 2- What is the exact reference for your [product_name]? 3- Which version of [product_name] SoftComfort are you using?

You mentioned that [product_name] can download its diagram to the [product_name], so communication seems fine. If the [document] transfer window doesn't show an interface, I suspect the [document] installation may be problematic. Try uninstalling [document] [version_no] and installing the latest [version_no].
Is [document] [version_no] available for standalone download? All I see is a bundle with [product_name] [version_no].
That's correct, it's not separately available for download. It's included as part of the [product_name] [version_no] upgrade installation. I'm unsure why [company_name] made it this way.

No, that didn't resolve it—the issue persists. I'm using Windows 10 Pro 64-bit. Firmware version on [product_name] is [version_no]. Could this be a firmware problem? Windows Firewall is fully disabled. Do [product_name] & [document] use different network ports? Thanks,

I don't think firmware is the problem, but I would suggest updating the firmware to [version_no] for your [product_name] device. My opinion is that the [document] installation isn't correct, as the transfer window doesn't show any interfaces. You might want to submit a support request directly to [company_name].

It looks like you haven't selected a working network card when downloading. If the dropdown list for network cards is empty, it means the software can't detect any network cards on your PC. Try running the [document] as an administrator. If it still doesn't work, consider reinstalling your network card drivers.

I've found that [product_name] connects successfully even without specifying an Ethernet adapter, which is strange since [document] doesn't behave the same way. It may be a Windows 10 or administrator permission issue. Thanks,
Did you manage to solve the problem? I'm facing the same issue and have tried everything. Thank you.
I encountered this issue too—the quickest solution was to remove the memory card, insert it into a card reader, and use the [document] to download to SD card. I still use this approach today.
Could you provide more details? Which [product_name] are you using? What steps have you tried so far? Simply saying you've tried everything doesn't give enough information.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing difficulty connecting the [document] to the [product_name] device over Ethernet, even though [product_name] establishes connections and downloads projects without issue. The lack of detected network interfaces in the [document] blocks transfers, leading to reliance on memory card workarounds that are cumbersome. The thread discusses issues like inconsistent software behavior, confusion regarding software versions, installation processes, and network card recognition. No successful resolution has been confirmed.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [document] to detect their network interface and connect with the [product_name] device over Ethernet similarly to [product_name], enabling easy project downloads without needing to physically handle the memory card.
